messages.author: 1ff63ac4948de366
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] probeset-level RMA summarized data and FIRMA group
parts:
Hi.

See comments below.

>
> qn <- QuantileNormalization(csBC, typesToUpdate="pm")
> csN <- process(qn, verbose=verbose)
>
> Then how to get the probeset data with labels(with probeset_id as row
> names, like a data frame)?

Just to clarify, do you want RMA summarization at the probeset level?
If so, you can use 'extractDataFrame' on a ChipEffectSet ... for
example:

plmEx <- ExonRmaPlm(csN, mergeGroups=FALSE)
fit(plmEx, verbose=verbose)
cesEx <- getChipEffectSet(plmEx)
ExFit <- extractDataFrame(cesEx, units=1:3, addNames=TRUE)

More details at:
http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/human-exon-array-analysis

> And for FIRMA,
>
> firma <- FirmaModel(plmEx)
> fit(firma, verbose=verbose)
> fs <- getFirmaScores(firma)
> exFirma <- extractDataFrame(fs,addNames=TRUE)
> exFirma[,6:ncol(exFirma)]<-log2(exFirma[,6:ncol(exFirma)])
> ....
>
> Suppose I have 100 samples which can be classified as 2 groups(50
> samples each group). After this step, how should I know which exon are
> differentially spliced in the two groups?

One way to do this would be to take the table of FIRMA scores (the
right most 100 columns of 'exFirma' above) and do a limma analysis (as
if you were looking for differential expression but operating directly
on the FIRMA scores).

Hope that helps.
Mark

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: probeset-level RMA summarized data and FIRMA group
parts: Hi Mohsen. More below.
On 19/11/2008, at 3:30 AM, Mohsen Khorshid wrote:

> Hello,
>
> Thank you very much for your answers.
>
> I have used the "core" version and it works thank you again. I could
> also save it in tab delimited file.
> Could you please explain these columns of the FIRMA score table:
> unitName
> groupName
> unit
> group
> cell

units = genes or transcript clusters
group = probeset (as defined by Affymetrix)

unitName is the identifier (what the identifier is depends on what CDF
you used), unit is just an index. groupName will by the Affymetrix-
defined probeset identifier, group is just an index. For FIRMA
scores, cell should always be 1 (I think).

> Is the unit corresponding to probesets?! How can I extract the
> expression level of an exon.

unit != probeset, at least not what Affy calls a probeset. Unit
corresponds to the collection of probesets for a transcript cluster.
Affy has probe selection regions (PSRs) which is roughly an exon, but
sometimes there are multiple probesets per exon.

You could get the probeset RMA summaries. From http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/human-exon-array-analysis
, it says:

-------------
...
There are two options, regardless of the kind of custom CDF you use.
To fit a summary of the entire transcript (i.e. estimate the overall
expression for the transcript), do:

plmTr <- ExonRmaPlm(csN, mergeGroups=TRUE)
print(plmTr)

Otherwise, to fit exon-by-exon, change the value of mergeGroups to
FALSE in the ExonRmaPlm() call above.

plmEx <- ExonRmaPlm(csN, mergeGroups=FALSE)
print(plmEx)
-------------

You can do the latter one and later on in that web page, it shows you
how to 'getChipEffectSet' and 'extractDataFrame' ...

> For example I would like to get the expression level of exon
> ENSE00000756202 in ENSG00000111780? How do you map the "unit ids" to
> "ensemble exon ids"?

This is tricky. But, its really just a matter of matching genome
coordinates. You'll need to know the coordinates of your ENSE, which
you can get from Biomart (or the biomaRt R package) and Affymetrix
gives you a file (CSV) of the coordinates of each probeset.

> About the visualization:
> I am sorry for confusion. I have been looking at GenomeGraphs about
> a week ago. This is mostly showing the exons of one transcript. What
> specifically I need is to generate the is to visualize the firma
> scores represented by colors in each CEL files for let's say 20
> transcripts.

OK, so you don't want plots like the supplementary data? How about
just extracting the matrix of FIRMA scores for those 20 transcripts
and using the 'image' command?

Hope that helps.

Mark
